surficial.description: Clay to silt-textured till (derived from glaciolacustrine deposits or shale). Regional literature calls this the Halton Till, but that name is not carried in the OGS layer attributes and was not verified here.
surficial.where: The inland plain north of the old Lake Iroquois shoreline: query points at the reference coordinate (43.5789, -79.6583), the Wikipedia city coordinate (43.6, -79.65), Erin Mills, Streetsville, Meadowvale and Malton all return unit 5d.

surficial.unit: OGS MRD128-REV unit 9c - Coarse-textured glaciolacustrine deposits
surficial.description: Sand, gravel, minor silt and clay; foreshore and basinal deposits of glacial Lake Iroquois.
surficial.where: The lakeshore band south of the Dundas Street alignment: query points at Port Credit, Lakeview, Clarkson and Lorne Park all return unit 9c. Wikipedia records that the former Glacial Lake Iroquois shoreline roughly follows the Dundas Street alignment, most prominent at the former brickyard on Shoreline Drive near Mavis Road.

surficial.description: Bedrock at or near surface (drift too thin to map).
surficial.where: Cooksville Creek corridor: the query point at Cooksville GO Station (43.58306, -79.62361) returns unit 3. Wikipedia notes the only other noticeable relief is the Credit River valley embankments and the Lake Iroquois shoreline.

bedrock.formation: Georgian Bay Formation across most of the city, with Queenston Formation in the west (Erin Mills, Meadowvale); both Upper Ordovician shale-dominated units (OGS MRD219).
bedrock.description: Georgian Bay: interbedded grey-green to dark grey shale and fossiliferous calcareous siltstone to bioclastic limestone; returned at the reference coordinate, the Wikipedia city coordinate, Port Credit, Lakeview, Clarkson, Lorne Park, Streetsville, Cooksville and Malton. Queenston: red shale and siltstone, minor green shale and siltstone, and variable calcareous siltstone to sandstone and limestone interbeds; returned at Erin Mills and Meadowvale. The contact therefore runs through the west of the city, west of the Credit River at Streetsville but east of Erin Mills.
bedrock.depth_note: Depth to bedrock was not retrieved (no drift-thickness dataset queried). OGS surficial mapping shows bedrock at or near surface (unit 3) at the Cooksville GO Station query point; elsewhere bedrock lies beneath till or glaciolacustrine sand of unstated thickness.

implications_for_piles: The City-hosted deck sample drawing (LMCBO Standard Details D01a-D01d, 2012) sets the conventional baseline: poured concrete piers a minimum of 1200 mm below grade on undisturbed soil, with bearing capacity determined prior to construction and the allowable pressure reduced by 50% where water is at or near the bottom of the footing excavation. The drawing does not mention helical piles, CCMC or BMEC; the City's deck drawing checklist requires the floor plan to state soil bearing capacity and the size, thickness and material of the foundation.

The same drawing's soil-bearing table spans 40 kPa (soft clay) to 200 kPa (till), 300 kPa (clay shale) and 500 kPa (sound rock), and general note 11 says to contact the local building department for local soil bearing capacities; no Mississauga-specific bearing values were retrieved.

Soil texture divides on the old Lake Iroquois shoreline along the Dundas Street alignment: OGS maps coarse sand and gravel (unit 9c) at Port Credit, Lakeview, Clarkson and Lorne Park, and clay-to-silt till (unit 5d) at Erin Mills, Streetsville, Meadowvale, Malton and the city centre, so any soil-specific design is not transferable between the lakeshore and the inland plain.

OGS maps bedrock at or near surface (unit 3) at the Cooksville GO Station query point over Georgian Bay shale; shallow shale is a site condition to confirm before installation along Cooksville Creek and the Credit River valley. No site-specific depth, torque or capacity figures were retrieved.

permits.authority: City of Mississauga Building Division (the City's fee schedule is titled 'Abbreviated Building Division Fees'; the web pages say 'the City' and 'City inspectors'; Building By-law 0236-2024 vests authority in the Chief Building Official)
permits.deck_permit_required_when: The City's 'When a building permit is required' page lists 'Deck greater than 0.61 metres (2 feet) high' under projects that need a permit and 'Deck less than 600 mm (2 feet) in height' under projects that don't. No separate area threshold is printed for decks; the same page lists 'Building or structure (other than a shed) greater than 10 square metres, or any size that contains plumbing' and 'Porch that's covered' as requiring a permit.
permits.footing_depth_requirement: City-hosted 'Deck Sample Drawing' (LMCBO Standard Details D01a-D01d, dated 2012): 'POURED CONCRETE PIER MIN. 1200mm BELOW GRADE ON UNDISTURBED SOIL'; 89x89 minimum wood post anchored to the concrete pier with a metal shoe and 12.7 mm bolt embedded 100 mm minimum; pier top 150 mm minimum above grade; pier sizes 200-600 mm diameter chosen from the supported deck area divided by the soil bearing capacity (table: soft clay 40 kPa, loose sand or gravel 50, firm clay 75, dense or compact silt 100, stiff clay 150, dense compact sand or gravel 150, till 200, clay shale 300, sound rock 500). General notes: piers shall bear on undisturbed soil with bearing capacity determined prior to construction; allowable bearing reduced by 50% with water at or near the bottom of the excavation; a deck is not permitted to be supported on brick veneer; free-standing decks over 600 mm above grade must resist lateral loading. The drawing says nothing about helical piles, CCMC, BMEC or an engineer's design; the deck checklist page requires the floor plan to show 'Soil bearing capacity' and 'Size, thickness and material specifications of foundation' and lists 'Schedule 1 Designer Information' as a required form.
inspections: Initial site inspection (City page: book before starting any construction work; it identifies which inspections apply and their order)
Footing - readiness to construct footings (Building By-law Schedule D)
Backfill - substantial completion of footings and foundations prior to commencement of backfilling (Schedule D)
Framing - substantial completion of structural framing (Schedule D)
Final (Schedule D lists Final (Plumbing), Final (HVAC) and Final (Completion of Occupied Building); the deck-specific final is assigned at the initial inspection)
permits.fee_note: Abbreviated Building Division Fees, Building By-law 0236-2024, effective February 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027, Schedule B 'Other Miscellaneous Work': 'Decks, porches, basement stairwell, etc. to houses $244.00 each'. Residential minimum permit fee $244; non-residential minimum $386; a $50 non-refundable electronic pre-screening fee is paid at online submission and credited toward the permit; revisions to reviewed plans $160/hour.
permits.timeline_note: City page: pre-screening usually takes about 7 to 10 business days; a complete residential application gets a first review in 10 business days; resubmissions have no guaranteed time and each cycle could add two or more weeks; average time to issue a residential alteration (detached, semi) permit is 7 weeks. Inspections run Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
permits.portal_note: All building permit applications must be submitted online through the City's ePlans portal; drawings are uploaded as individual greyscale landscape PDFs named to match the title block (for example 'A01 SITE PLAN').
